items.passage:
The new-comer was perhaps some four years older than the other, but this was only detected by close examination.

“And so you have come at last. O brother, brother! how I have wanted you!” said Louis, drawing his guest to a sofa, and shaking hands with him over and over again. “You have no idea how very, very much I have wanted you!”

A shade of trouble came over his face as he spoke, and instantly that of his brother darkened with the same shadow, as if the pain which one felt must have a mutual vibration.
items.question: Based on the text, which choice best describes the relationship between Louis and his guest?
options: They are business partners who meet only to settle an old dispute.
They are brothers whose close bond lets each share the other's feelings.
They are old rivals who hide their resentment behind warm greetings.
They are strangers who have just been introduced by a mutual friend.
items.explanation: Louis가 손님을 'O brother, brother!'라고 부르며 몹시 기다렸다고 말하므로 두 사람은 형제이다. 또한 Louis의 얼굴에 걱정이 스치자 형의 얼굴도 즉시 같은 그늘로 어두워졌다는 서술은 서로의 감정을 함께 느끼는 깊은 유대를 보여 준다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. A, C, D는 사업 관계·숨은 적대감·처음 만난 사이를 말하지만 지문의 애정 어린 재회 장면과 맞지 않는다.

items.passage:
Is the best Gothic fit for our worship? Does it express our belief? Or shall we choose some other style?

I say that it is; and that it is so because it is a style which, if not founded on Nature, has taken into itself more of Nature, of Nature beautiful and healthy, than any other style.

With greater knowledge of Nature, both geographical and scientific, fresh styles of architecture may and will arise, as much more beautiful, and as much more natural, than the Gothic, as Gothic is more beautiful and natural than the Norman. Till then we must take the best models which we have; use them; and, as it were, use them up and exhaust them.
items.question: Based on the text, how does the author view the relationship between Gothic architecture and the styles that may follow it?
options: Gothic is a perfect style that no later style could ever surpass.
Later styles should be avoided because they reject Gothic models.
Gothic is the best current model but may be surpassed by later styles.
Gothic and Norman styles are equally natural and equally beautiful.
items.explanation: 필자는 고딕이 다른 양식보다 자연을 더 많이 담았기에 예배에 맞는다고 말한다. 동시에 자연에 대한 지식이 늘면 고딕보다 더 아름답고 자연스러운 새 양식이 생길 것이라고 예상하며, 그때까지는 가진 최선의 모델을 쓰자고 한다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. A는 미래 양식의 가능성을 부정하고, B는 새 양식을 피하라는 주장이 없으며, D는 고딕이 노르만보다 더 아름답다는 서술과 어긋난다.

items.passage:
I was ambitious to absorb all the wisdom I could, but, really, I could not give an intelligent report of the points under discussion at any sitting. Oliver Johnson asked me, one day, if I enjoyed them. I thought, from a twinkle in his eye, that he thought I did not, so I told him I was ashamed to confess that I did not know what they were talking about. He said, "Neither do I,--very few of their hearers do,--so you need not be surprised that they are incomprehensible to you, nor think less of your own capacity."

I was indebted to Mr. Johnson for several of the greatest pleasures I enjoyed in Boston.
items.question: Based on the text, which choice best describes the relationship between the narrator and Oliver Johnson?
options: Johnson mocks the narrator for failing to follow the discussions.
The narrator resents Johnson for exposing her confusion to others.
Johnson and the narrator compete to seem the most learned listener.
Johnson reassures the narrator, who later feels grateful to him.
items.explanation: 화자가 토론 내용을 이해하지 못했다고 고백하자 Johnson은 자신도 모르겠다며 화자의 능력을 낮게 보지 말라고 위로한다. 이어 화자는 보스턴에서 누린 큰 즐거움 여럿을 Johnson 덕분이라고 말한다. 따라서 위로와 감사의 관계를 말한 D가 정답이다. A의 조롱, B의 원망, C의 경쟁은 지문의 다정한 대화와 맞지 않는다.

items.passage:
The sweet fresh morning air seemed to revive her. Day was just breaking, and the sky was tinged all over with a soft rosy hue.

As she stood gazing on the still and peaceful scene before her, she heard the garden gate open, and a minute afterwards there was a gentle tap at the cottage door. The window of Katie's room was at the side of the house, so that Mrs. Lawrence could not see any one as they came through the garden. She glanced at the bed; Katie was still calmly sleeping. And opening the door as noiselessly as possible, she went down the stairs, thinking that perhaps the doctor had sent to inquire after his patient.
items.question: In the text, the breaking day with its soft rosy sky most likely symbolizes
options: a hopeful sense of renewal after a long night of watching.
the arrival of a dangerous visitor at the cottage door.
Mrs. Lawrence's wish to leave the cottage and its troubles.
the doctor's growing worry about the condition of his patient.
items.explanation: 상쾌한 아침 공기가 그녀를 되살리는 듯했고 하늘이 부드러운 장밋빛으로 물들었다는 묘사는 회복과 희망의 분위기를 만든다. 또 Katie가 여전히 평온하게 잠들어 있다는 서술은 밤새 간호한 뒤의 안도감을 뒷받침한다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B의 위험한 방문객, C의 떠나고 싶은 마음, D의 의사의 걱정은 지문에 근거가 없다.

items.passage: One cold, raw evening, Gwendoline, returning from a reception, entered her apartments through the sitting-room. She found it dark, and, hearing Alice in the bed-chamber, passed on, and, giving her wraps into her hands, returned to the sitting-room. She was shivering from the cold, and, going to the fire, stirred it to a blaze. The brightness illuminated floor and ceiling, chairs and table, falling on the black marble of the last-mentioned article of furniture, and upon the whiteness of a visiting card that lay like a snowflake before her, as she stood with her back to the chimney. Leaning over, she took it up, and turned it to the light behind her.
items.question: In the text, the white visiting card lying like a snowflake on the black marble most likely symbolizes
options: the warmth Gwendoline feels after returning to her bright fire.
an unexpected and possibly chilling message awaiting Gwendoline.
the comfort of Alice's steady service in the bed-chamber.
the pleasant memories Gwendoline brings home from the reception.
items.explanation: Gwendoline은 춥고 음산한 저녁에 떨며 돌아왔고, 불빛 아래 검은 대리석 위에 눈송이처럼 놓인 흰 명함을 발견한다. 어둠 속에서 갑자기 드러나는 눈송이 비유는 예상치 못한, 차가운 기운의 소식을 암시한다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. A는 불의 따뜻함을, C는 하녀를, D는 연회의 기억을 말하지만 명함이라는 이미지의 의미와 관련이 없다.

items.passage: A pair have built in a large, hollow limb in my old apple-tree for many years. Whether it is the same pair or not I do not know. Probably it is, or else some of their descendants. I looked into the cavity one day while the mother bird was upon the nest, but before she had laid any eggs. A sudden explosive sound came up out of the dark depths of the limb, much like that made by an alarmed cat. It made me jerk my head back, when out came the bird and hurried off.
items.question: In the text, the hollow limb of the old apple tree mainly serves as a symbol of
options: the author's fear of the dangers hidden in his orchard.
the decline of the old apple tree as it slowly dies.
a lasting home that birds return to year after year.
the author's wish to keep wild birds away from his house.
items.explanation: 필자는 한 쌍의 새가 여러 해 동안 그 늙은 사과나무의 빈 가지에 둥지를 틀었다고 말한다. 같은 쌍인지 그 후손인지는 모르지만 아마 그럴 것이라는 추측은 세대를 이어 돌아오는 보금자리라는 의미를 강조한다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. A의 두려움, B의 나무의 죽음, D의 새를 쫓으려는 마음은 지문에 드러나지 않는다.

items.passage:
Behind the throne is a female figure as if in attendance on the great god. The whole group is surrounded by hieroglyphics, and inclosed in a frame richly adorned with symbolical figures. The winged globe is above, with the wings spread over all, and a line of serpents crowns the whole. The figures and paintings are in such perfect preservation, that they give the most correct idea of their ornaments and decorations (See Plate 19).

Straight forward is the entrance into another chamber with two pillars. The wall of this place is outlined, ready for the sculptor to cut out his figure. It is here that we may plainly see the manner in which the artist prepared the figure on the wall ready to be cut; and it is almost impossible to give a description of the various figures, which adorn the walls and pillars of this chamber.
items.question: In the text, the outlined but uncut wall in the second chamber mainly serves as a sign of
options: the damage that time has done to the ancient paintings.
the great god's power over the figures that surround him.
the visitors' failure to understand the hieroglyphics.
the hidden working methods of the ancient artists.
items.explanation: 필자는 첫 방의 그림이 완벽하게 보존되어 있다고 설명한 뒤, 다음 방의 벽은 조각가가 새길 수 있도록 윤곽만 그려져 있다고 말한다. 이어 여기서 예술가가 벽에 형상을 준비한 방식을 분명히 볼 수 있다고 덧붙인다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. A는 보존 상태가 완벽하다는 서술과 어긋나고, B와 C는 미완성 벽의 의미와 관련이 없다.

items.passage: The feeling gave her a certain sense of exhilaration. From the depths of her despair her easily influenced spirits sprang again to hope and confidence. After all, nothing very dreadful had happened. She must struggle not to give way to intemperate feelings. She must bear with Polly! she must put up with Maggie. It was all very trying, of course, but it was the English way. She walked along faster and faster, and now her lips rose in a light song, and now again she ran, eager to get over the ground. When she ran her light hair floated behind her, and she looked less and less like a living creature.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “her easily influenced spirits sprang again to hope” most nearly suggests that she
options: quickly recovers her cheerfulness after feeling deep despair.
jumps up into the air out of a sudden fright.
is persuaded by Polly and Maggie to change her plans.
slowly loses all confidence as she walks along the road.
items.explanation: 이 구절 바로 앞에 절망의 깊은 곳에서라는 표현이 있고, 뒤에는 결국 끔찍한 일은 없었다는 생각이 이어진다. 그녀가 가볍게 노래하고 달리는 모습도 기분이 빠르게 회복되었음을 보여 준다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B는 비유를 문자 그대로 읽었고, C는 근거가 없으며, D는 지문의 흐름과 반대이다.

items.passage:
During all the years of his growth into manhood, ever since he could remember, he had been practically the only son, the “young squire” in the eyes of the peasantry. He felt cheated of his birthright.

The packing-up had been a terrible business. Nothing had been said about retaining his rooms, and his nature was one that shrank back before the shadow of a coming hint. Quietly he had put all his things together, turning from Ursula’s silent, terrified gaze. Silence seemed to have fallen upon them all like a paralysis. The servants looked at each other.

All his life had been sheltered too warmly in his father’s fostering affection. The luxury of his youth hung about him--the easy generosity which had accounted money only a thing to spend on himself or on others, according to requirement.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “fallen upon them all like a paralysis” most nearly suggests that the household
options: has become physically ill from the stress of the move.
is frozen into a tense, helpless stillness by events.
is calmly resting after the hard work of packing.
has agreed to ignore the young man's departure.
items.explanation: 짐 싸기가 끔찍한 일이었다는 서술과 Ursula의 겁에 질린 침묵의 시선은 집안의 긴장을 보여 준다. 하인들이 말없이 서로 쳐다보기만 했다는 점도 모두가 아무 말도 행동도 못 하는 상태임을 뒷받침한다. 따라서 마비처럼 내려앉은 침묵은 긴장된 무력함을 뜻하므로 B가 정답이다. A는 비유를 실제 질병으로 읽었고, C의 평온함과 D의 합의는 지문과 맞지 않는다.

items.passage:
"At length it came over a beautiful scene,
That nature in silence had made;
The place was but small, but't was sweetly serene,
And chequered with sunshine and shade.

"I gazed and I envied with painful good will,
And grew tired of my seat in the air;
When all of a sudden my Castle stood still,
As if some attraction were there.

"Like a lark from the sky it came fluttering down,
And placed me exactly in view,
When whom should I meet in this charming retreat
This corner of calmness, but--you.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “This corner of calmness” most nearly suggests
options: a crowded spot where the speaker feels trapped.
a sharp angle in the walls of the speaker's castle.
a small, peaceful place set apart from the world.
a cold, dark refuge from the heat of the sun.
items.explanation: 시의 앞부분은 이곳을 자연이 고요 속에 만든 작고도 평온한 장소로 묘사한다. 이어 화자는 이곳을 매력적인 은신처라고 부른 뒤 같은 장소를 고요의 구석이라고 다시 표현한다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. A의 혼잡함, B의 성벽 모서리라는 문자적 해석, D의 춥고 어두운 곳은 햇빛과 그늘이 어우러진 평온한 장면과 맞지 않는다.

items.passage: The occasional sense of our being too weak for the ordinary incidents of life, is strangely distressing. The cry of an infant makes us wretched for hours after, in spite of every effort of reason. I saw, through my telescope, two big boys worrying a little one, and I could not look to see the end of it. They were so far off that there was nothing to be done. The distress to me was such--the picture of the lives of the three boys was so vivid--that I felt as if I had no reason nor courage left.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “too weak for the ordinary incidents of life” most nearly suggests feeling
options: physically ill from a lack of rest and food.
unable to lift heavy objects in daily work.
too young to understand the actions of others.
emotionally overwhelmed by common painful sights.
items.explanation: 필자는 아기의 울음이 이성의 노력에도 몇 시간 동안 자신을 비참하게 만든다고 말한다. 또 망원경으로 큰 소년들이 작은 아이를 괴롭히는 장면을 보고 이성도 용기도 남지 않은 듯했다고 고백한다. 따라서 이 구절은 흔한 고통스러운 장면에 감정적으로 압도되는 상태를 뜻하므로 D가 정답이다. A와 B는 신체적 약함으로, C는 나이로 잘못 해석했다.

items.passage:
The family living in the hut consisted of three persons--man, wife and their little daughter, a sweet child of about four years of age. Both mother and child were neatly dressed, and had a genteel appearance that was in marked contrast with their surroundings. The child wore a tidy pink dress, tastefully ornamented, and seemed as if she had just come from the class-room of a convent school. The family impressed us as having seen better days, and had evidently not lived always so far away from their fellows.

Near the house stood a large calabash tree, bearing the largest fruit of the kind we had yet observed.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “as if she had just come from the class-room of a convent school” most nearly suggests that the child
options: looks unusually neat and cared for given her setting.
has recently arrived from a school far from her home.
is shy and silent in the presence of strangers.
is dressed in a plain uniform like other pupils.
items.explanation: 지문은 엄마와 아이가 단정하게 차려입어 주변 환경과 뚜렷이 대조되는 품위 있는 모습이었다고 말한다. 아이가 단정하고 멋스럽게 장식된 분홍 옷을 입었다는 묘사도 이 비유를 뒷받침한다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B는 비유를 사실로 읽었고, C의 수줍음은 근거가 없으며, D의 수수한 교복은 장식된 분홍 옷과 맞지 않는다.

items.passage: Venus, who was present at the festival, heard him and knew the thought he would have uttered; and as an omen of her favor, caused the flame on the altar to shoot up thrice in a fiery point into the air. When he returned home, he went to see his statue, and leaning over the couch, gave a kiss to the mouth. It seemed to be warm. He pressed its lips again, he laid his hand upon the limbs; the ivory felt soft to his touch and yielded to his fingers like the wax of Hymettus. While he stands astonished and glad, though doubting, and fears he may be mistaken, again and again with a lover's ardor he touches the object of his hopes. It was indeed alive!
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “yielded to his fingers like the wax of Hymettus” most nearly suggests that
options: the statue breaks apart when he presses it firmly.
the hard ivory turns soft and pliant like living flesh.
the statue is melting from the heat of the altar flame.
the ivory feels sticky and unpleasant to his hand.
items.explanation: 그가 입맞춤했을 때 조각상이 따뜻하게 느껴졌고, 상아가 손길에 부드럽게 느껴졌다는 서술이 이어진다. 마지막에 조각상이 정말 살아 있었다고 밝혀지므로 밀랍 비유는 단단한 상아가 살아 있는 몸처럼 부드러워졌음을 뜻한다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. A의 부서짐, C의 녹아내림, D의 불쾌함은 기쁨과 놀라움의 장면과 맞지 않는다.

items.passage: At the dinner-table, her father again sat eying his guest with that same cold look of distrust and suspicion. And when the meal was at an end, he rose abruptly and called his daughter into another room. Presently Ralph heard his angry voice resounding through the house, interrupted now and then by a woman’s sobs, and a subdued, passionate pleading. When Bertha again entered the room, her eyes were very red, and he saw that she had been weeping. She threw a shawl over her shoulders, beckoned to him with her hand, and he arose and followed her. She led the way silently until they reached a thick copse of birch and alder near the strand. She dropped down upon a bench between two trees, and he took his seat at her side.
items.question: As used in the text, what does the word “subdued” most nearly mean?
options: defeated
obedient
hushed
gloomy
items.explanation: 아버지의 화난 목소리가 집 안에 울려 퍼졌고, 그 사이로 여자의 흐느낌과 억눌린 간청이 끼어들었다는 맥락이다. 큰 소리와 대비되는 낮고 조용한 소리를 가리키므로 subdued는 '낮춘, 소리를 죽인'이라는 뜻이다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. A의 '패배한', B의 '순종적인', D의 '우울한'은 이 문맥에서 소리의 크기를 나타내지 못한다.

items.passage: The words have certainly not changed since he last glanced at them; and yet they seem to him to have a more compelling look. Why can't he force them to be more explicit? He pauses; telegram in one hand and candle in the other. What can she want with him? It is just within the bounds of possibility that she may really need his presence; how or why, he is unable to hazard the faintest conjecture. But it is just within the limits of the possible that she may. Various suggestions of what shape that possible may take flit across his puzzled brain. Can it be that her husband has at length made the discovery of what for five years has been the open secret of all his acquaintance?
items.question: As used in the text, what does the word “hazard” most nearly mean?
options: endanger
gamble
damage
venture
items.explanation: 그는 그녀가 왜 자신을 필요로 하는지 전혀 알 수 없어 당황하고 있다. 뒤에서 여러 가능성이 그의 머릿속을 스친다는 서술이 이어지므로 hazard는 추측을 '감히 내놓다'라는 뜻이다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. A의 '위험에 빠뜨리다', B의 '도박하다', C의 '손상시키다'는 추측을 시도하는 맥락과 맞지 않는다.

items.passage:
Time passed on, and the Fairies had done nothing to gain their lovely home again. They wept no longer, but watched little Bud, as she daily tended the flowers, restoring their strength and beauty, or with gentle words flew from nest to nest, teaching the little birds to live happily together; and wherever she went blessings fell, and loving hearts were filled with gratitude.

Then, one by one, the Elves secretly did some little work of kindness, and found a quiet joy come back to repay them. Flowers looked lovingly up as they passed, birds sang to cheer them when sad thoughts made them weep. And soon little Bud found out their gentle deeds, and her friendly words gave them new strength.
items.question: As used in the text, what does the word “tended” most nearly mean?
options: cared for
leaned toward
listened to
grew tired of
items.explanation: Bud가 매일 꽃을 돌보면서 그 힘과 아름다움을 되살렸다는 맥락이다. 그녀가 가는 곳마다 축복이 내렸다는 서술도 보살핌의 의미를 뒷받침하므로 tended는 '돌보다'라는 뜻이다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B의 '기울다', C의 '귀 기울이다', D의 '싫증 나다'는 꽃을 되살리는 행동과 연결되지 않는다.

items.passage:
I by no means think graceful manners of small importance. They are the outward form of refinement in the mind, and good affections in the heart; and as such must be lovely. But when the form exists without the vital principle within, it is as cold and lifeless as flowers carved in marble.

Politeness, either of feeling or of manner, can never be taught by set maxims. Every-day influence, so unconsciously exerted, is all important in forming the characters of children: and in nothing more important than in their manners. If you are habitually polite, your children will become so, by the mere force of imitation, without any specific directions on the subject.
items.question: As used in the text, what does the word “set” most nearly mean?
options: placed
fixed
ready
hardened
items.explanation: 필자는 예의가 정해진 격언으로는 결코 가르쳐질 수 없고 일상의 무의식적 영향과 모방으로 길러진다고 말한다. 미리 정해 둔 규칙과 대비되므로 set은 '고정된, 정해진'이라는 뜻이다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. A의 '놓인', C의 '준비된', D의 '굳은'은 격언을 수식하는 이 문맥에서 자연스럽지 않다.

items.passage:
Making my way to where I supposed headquarters to be, I saw an important looking individual near by, whom I addressed, and inquired if he could tell me where General McClellan was to be found? "No, I can not." Could he tell me when he was expected at headquarters? "No." Was there any person there of whom I could inquire? "Not a person." Did he know of any place where the necessary information could be obtained? "Not a place." Could he make any suggestion, or throw the least ray of light upon the subject, which might lead to the whereabouts of the general? "Not the slightest."

Turning away in disgust, I said to the man, "Well, good-by, Mr. Negative. I hope the effort which you have made to assist me will not injure you mentally or physically;" and so saying I rode away, feeling that if I was as big as he imagined himself, and as strong as he was indifferent, I would give him a vigorous shaking before leaving him.
items.question: As used in the text, what does the word “indifferent” most nearly mean?
options: mediocre
neutral
unconcerned
impartial
items.explanation: 그 남자는 화자의 모든 질문에 '아니요', '전혀요'로만 짧게 답하며 도우려는 의지를 보이지 않는다. 화자가 그를 Mr. Negative라 부르며 비꼬는 장면도 그의 무관심을 강조하므로 indifferent는 '무관심한'이라는 뜻이다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. A의 '평범한', B의 '중립적인', D의 '공정한'은 도움을 거부하는 태도를 정확히 나타내지 못한다.

items.passage: The cries of the spectators cheered Hippomenes,--"Now, now, do your best! haste, haste! you gain on her! relax not! one more effort!" It was doubtful whether the youth or the maiden heard these cries with the greater pleasure. But his breath began to fail him, his throat was dry, the goal yet far off. At that moment he threw down one of the golden apples. The virgin was all amazement. She stopped to pick it up. Hippomenes shot ahead. Shouts burst forth from all sides. She redoubled her efforts, and soon overtook him.
items.question: As used in the text, what does the word “redoubled” most nearly mean?
options: repeated
folded
doubted
intensified
items.explanation: Hippomenes가 사과를 던져 앞서 나가자, 그녀는 노력을 redoubled하여 곧 그를 따라잡는다. 다시 따라잡았다는 결과는 그녀가 더 힘껏 달렸음을 뜻하므로 redoubled는 '강화하다'라는 의미이다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. A의 '반복하다'는 노력의 증가를 담지 못하고, B의 '접다'와 C의 '의심하다'는 문맥과 관계가 없다.

items.passage:
Meantime, the unconscious object of their criticism walked sadly down the old market-garden, whose rude outlines and homely details he once clothed with the poetry of a sensitive man's first love. Well, it was a common cabbage field and potato patch after all. In his disgust he felt conscious of even the loss of that sense of patronage and superiority which had invested his affection for a girl of meaner condition. His self-respect was humiliated with his love. The soil and dirt of those wretched cabbages had clung to him, but not to her. It was she who had gone higher; it was he who was left in the vulgar ruins of his misplaced passion.

He reached the bottom of the garden without observing any sign of the lonely invalid.
items.question: Which choice best describes the shift in tone in the text?
options: It moves from cheerful excitement to calm acceptance of his love.
It moves from anger at the girl to sympathy for her poor family.
It moves from bored description to eager hope for the future.
It moves from fond memory of the garden to bitter disillusionment.
items.explanation: 지문 앞부분은 그가 한때 첫사랑의 시정으로 그 텃밭을 감쌌다고 회상한다. 그러나 곧 그것은 결국 흔한 양배추 밭이었다는 문장으로 어조가 바뀌고, 그는 잘못된 열정의 초라한 폐허에 남겨졌다고 느낀다. 따라서 애틋한 기억에서 쓰라린 환멸로 바뀐다는 D가 정답이다. A의 평온한 수용, B의 동정, C의 희망은 굴욕과 혐오의 감정과 맞지 않는다.
